findings.description: A long-lived AWS access key ID and secret access key are embedded in plaintext in the Lambda function's environment variables and committed to source control. Any principal with lambda:GetFunctionConfiguration, console read access, or repository access can retrieve and reuse these credentials directly.

findings.issue_category: missing CMK encryption of environment variables
findings.description: No kms_key_arn is specified, so the environment variables - which hold secrets - are protected only by the default AWS-managed key and are returned in cleartext by the console and API to any principal with function read permissions. A customer-managed CMK with a restricted key policy would impose a separate authorization boundary on the secret material.

The function targets the nodejs12.x runtime, which is past end of support and no longer receives security patches from AWS, leaving the execution environment exposed to known unpatched vulnerabilities.

The function declares no vpc_config, so it executes outside any customer VPC with unrestricted outbound internet access and no security group or NACL boundary. Combined with the static credentials in its environment, this leaves an unconstrained egress path for data exfiltration if the function is compromised.

The trust policy grants sts:AssumeRole to the lambda.amazonaws.com service principal with no aws:SourceAccount or aws:SourceArn condition, so it is not scoped to a specific function or owning account and offers no confused-deputy protection.
